correctness_confidence.basis: Formal verification of 18 theorems in Lean 4 with zero axioms, zero sorry, and zero warnings provides exceptional algebraic and logical soundness across all trichotomy, KKT, and mean-payoff certificates.

novelty.basis: First machine-checked exact-Q soundness and mutual exclusivity certification for OpenAI's linear programming trichotomy, coupled with explicit staircase circuit-imbalance amplification up to 10^180.

reproducibility.basis: Complete zero-dependency Lean 4 source files and pure-stdlib Python verifier scripts with 16 test certificates covering four distinct algorithmic modes.

rigor.basis: Rigorous algebraic proofs of support partitioning, diagonal price-rescaling orthogonality invariance, and KKT square-completion optimality with comprehensive red-teaming.

significance.basis: Resolves the critical certification companion problem for strongly polynomial algorithms in linear programming, convex QP, and mean-payoff games without floating-point trust.

potential_errors: Scope boundary restricts Python verifier matrix dimensions to MAX_DIM = 64, requiring future extensions for larger sparse systems.
strengths: Flawless zero-dependency Lean 4 formalization with 0 sorry and 0 warnings.
Comprehensive 16-certificate test atlas spanning LP trichotomy, unbounded rays, Farkas infeasibility, convex QP KKT, and mean-payoff game saddles.
Rigorous adversarial red-teaming suite rejecting 52/52 malicious attacks.
strong_novelty_candidates: Staircase circuit-imbalance amplification family An(M) demonstrating exact geometric growth and bit-length separation.
Machine-checked exact-Z/Q soundness and mutual exclusivity for primal-dual trichotomy.
summary: The manuscript establishes exact-Z/Q soundness, mutual exclusivity, and scale-separation theorems for OpenAI's strongly polynomial linear programming trichotomy, convex quadratic programming, and mean-payoff games. Backed by an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 formalization and a pure-stdlib Python verifier, the work successfully certifies an atlas of 16 exact-Q certificates with zero floating-point reliance.
weaknesses: Dependence on external solver outputs (OpenAI's algorithm) for certificate generation, though verified independently via exact rational arithmetic.
